slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides, the legs. The angle between them is the vertex angle; the other two are base angles.

Isosceles Triangle Theorem: if two sides of a triangle are equal, the angles opposite them are equal.

Proof: in triangle ABC with AB = AC, draw the bisector of angle A meeting BC at D. Triangles ABD and ACD have AB = AC, angle BAD = angle CAD, and AD = AD, so they are congruent by SAS. Then angle B = angle C by CPCTC.
